subject: C988A6875D85E5BE715D95DDF7075DB4
introduction: “O Lord! Make us steadfast in Thy Covenant and Testament.” After Bahá’u’lláh’s passing His community was tested by the rebellion of members of His own family, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote these prayers, for individuals, households and the whole body of believers, asking that feet be made firm, hearts guarded from doubt, and what had been scattered be gathered. The Psalmist prays the same way: “Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not”; Paul’s letters urge “be ye stedfast, unmoveable” and “stand fast”; the Qur’an says to “hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate”; and Jesus prayed “that they all may be one”. Elijah’s “I, even I only, am left” is the voice of reading 110. Emerson’s self-trust and Milton’s warning against being “a heretic in the truth” ask what distinguishes steadfastness from mere immovability.
questions: What do these prayers assume a person is in danger of? What, in the image of feet slipping, is the slope?
Many of the prayers ask firmness for someone else, or for “us”. Why is steadfastness treated as something a community asks for together?
Emerson says “trust thyself”; these prayers ask to hold to a Covenant. What does each protect against?
Milton warns that one can hold the truth for bad reasons. What would it look like to be firm in a covenant thoughtfully?
Reading 2 asks that what is scattered be gathered and what is torn be mended. Is firmness the cause of unity or its result?

outside.why: “Grant that all may stand firm and steadfast.” Be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.
“Unite all that is scattered … and mend all that is torn.” He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
The prayer of Jesus on the night of his arrest: that they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee.
“Make firm my steps.” Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.
My Refuge, my Shelter. In the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion; he shall set me up upon a rock.
Make us firm in Thy straight path. Show us the straight path, the path of those whom Thou hast favoured.
Our Lord! Cause not our hearts to stray after Thou hast guided us.
“Make us steadfast in Thy Covenant and Testament.” The faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him.
Expand his breast. He whose bosom Allah hath expanded, so that he followeth a light from his Lord.
Make firm the feet of Thy loved ones. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; for he is faithful that promised.
Strengthen him to remain firm. Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
Firm on the path “whereon feet have slipped”. But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.
Steadfast in Thy love. Neither death, nor life, nor things present, nor things to come, shall be able to separate us from the love of God.
Praise for having been guided, and a prayer to continue. He which hath begun a good work in you will perform it.
Make me detached from all else. I count all things but loss.
Assist Thy servants to hold together. Hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate.
Grant growth to these saplings. Like a tree planted by the rivers of water; his leaf also shall not wither.
Firm in Thy straight path and ancient Covenant. That ye, being rooted and grounded in love, may be able to comprehend.
Guard their hearts from the doubts of the heedless. He that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
That we be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine.
Firm, with her children and descendants. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Nourished in the faith from his tender years. Continue thou in the things which thou hast learned; from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures.
Assist this handmaid to serve those who are steadfast. Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers.
Strengthen Thy servants who are firm. Fear thou not; for I am with thee: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will uphold thee.
Strengthen their backs. They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength.
Make firm his steps, expand his breast. Uphold me with thy free spirit.
Through him make hearts steadfast. When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
By those who circled round the throne of Thy will. Seeing we are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with patience the race that is set before us.
Strengthen my limbs to arise in Thy service. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
By those who have not broken Thy Covenant. My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips.
Adorn my heart with Thy love and my tongue with Thy remembrance. These words shall be in thine heart; and thou shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house.
Illumine the eyes; let the ears hear. The eyes of your understanding being enlightened.
Faithful and steadfast “amidst all peoples”. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods.
By this Exile driven from His native land. They confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
That the veils of the world shall not prevent me. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
Steadfast so that the clamour of the peoples shall not move me. We ought to obey God rather than men.

Emerson on standing against the crowd’s clamour: trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string. He means the self; the prayer means a covenant outside the self. Which makes a person harder to move?
“The oppressed ‘Abdu’l-Bahá has fallen into the hands of the people of discord.” Elijah: the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant; and I, even I only, am left.
Every evening I lament, and every morning I call out. Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud.
Preserve him in the cave of Thy protection. He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
“Make firm my steps on the path of agreement.” That there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind.
Beseech Him every morn and eve to make thee firm. Praying always with all prayer and supplication, and watching thereunto with all perseverance.
Assist Thy loved ones through Thy mighty stronghold. The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
Send down a tranquillity from Thy presence. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.

“Make me a herald of the Covenant, and a piercing flame against the people of discord.” Milton feared the firmness that never examines itself: a man may be a heretic in the truth, if he believes things only because his pastor says so. What keeps firmness in a covenant from becoming that?
Those who have cast the world behind them. Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee.
The Book calls to the Covenant. Whosoever surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good, he verily hath grasped the firm hand-hold.
Firm on the most upright path. Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.
Praise for feet “firmly fixed upon the Covenant”. Unto him that is able to keep you from falling.
A band who supplicate to the Kingdom of Thy mercy. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.
A tongue of lowliness and a heart free from pride. God be merciful to me a sinner.

shortfall: These hundred prayers ask one thing, firmness in the Covenant, in closely similar words for many persons; companions were given to the images that vary (the slipping foot, the scattered flock, the stronghold, the wavering heart) and half the prayers were left to share them.
